subject: AI & Agents
title: Why Hype Cycles Repeat
description: A fast breakdown of Why Hype Cycles Repeat for builders.

hook.text: Every decade promises 'AI will change everything in five years.' Every decade is wrong — so far.

buildup.text: The pattern: breakthrough → media frenzy → wild promises → reality check → funding collapse.

discovery.text: Gartner calls it the 'hype cycle' — peak of inflated expectations, then a trough of disillusionment.

twist.text: After each winter, the surviving ideas became foundations for the next wave.

climax.text: Backpropagation survived the winters. So did reinforcement learning. So did neural nets.

punchline.text: The hype dies. The science doesn't.

quiz.question: What is the typical AI hype cycle pattern?

details.summary: AI has gone through repeated cycles of hype and disappointment because each breakthrough sparks extrapolation beyond what the technology can deliver. Understanding this pattern prevents being caught off guard.
details.whyItMatters: Recognizing hype cycles helps investors, workers, and policymakers make grounded decisions. The current AI boom follows familiar patterns, and awareness is the best defense against unrealistic expectations.
takeaways: AI hype cycles follow a predictable boom-bust pattern
Each breakthrough triggers overestimation of near-term capability
Historical awareness helps navigate current AI expectations

faq.question: Why does AI hype keep recurring?
faq.answer: Each genuine breakthrough makes further progress seem inevitable and imminent. Media amplifies success stories while ignoring limitations. Investors and executives extrapolate linearly from exponential-seeming progress.

faq.question: Is the current AI boom headed for another winter?
faq.answer: Some correction is likely as commercial expectations meet reality. However, the current boom has stronger fundamentals — massive data, proven applications, and real revenue — than previous cycles.
